newsitem.title: CONGO: South Africa says Kabila headed for Zaire talks.
newsitem.headline: South Africa says Kabila headed for Zaire talks.

text.p: South Africa said on Saturday Zaire's rebel leader Laurent Kabila was heading for talks at sea with President Mobutu Sese Seko.

"Kabila is at Soyo (in Angola), (South African Deputy President) Thabo Mbeki is landing there now, he is expected to bring Kabila to the ship within the next hour," South African deputy foreign minister Aziz Pahad told reporters on the converted icebreaker SAS Outeniqua, moored in Congo's port of Pointe Noire.
Pahad said Mobutu would arrive on board the ship after Kabila and that talks were likely to take much longer than had previously been expected.

"(South African) President Nelson Mandela is willing to stay as long as possible," Pahad said, adding that the agenda for the talks would be based on a peace plan developed by the United Nations and Organisation of African Unity.
Mandela said he was disappointed that talks had not begun on Friday as planned.
"I am convinced that in Mobutu and Kabila, Zaire has two sons who have the capacity to be equal to the challenge of taking their country forward," Mandela told reporters.
